title: Lineage and Early Formation of Shyam Singh

blocks.text: The author introduces this new cycle with a personal claim of authority, saying he heard it from my own mother because she was descended from Shyam Singh's household. That framing turns the page into a family-backed remembrance rather than a distant chronicle.

It then traces the line through Mali, a Sandhu Jat at village Narla, and explains how the young Shyam Singh came under the influence of Mastan Singh and the Khalsa discipline around him. The story emphasizes initiation, inherited service, and the shaping of character in a martial but devout community.

By the close of the page, Shyam Singh is no longer only a named ancestor. He stands as the worthy heir to a disciplined tradition in which hospitality, courage, and readiness to initiate into the Khalsa Panth are treated as marks of legitimacy.
